# Travel Insurance Checklist (Schengen-Compliant)

Travel insurance is **mandatory** for a Schengen visa. A non-compliant or unclear certificate is one of the most common avoidable rejection reasons.

> **Authoritative reference:** Schengen visa code, Article 15. The current Schengen-area medical-cost minimum is **€30,000**, valid in **all 29 Schengen countries**, covering the **entire planned stay**.

---

## Hard requirements (your certificate must say all of these)

| Requirement | What it must say | ✓ |
|---|---|---|
| **Coverage amount** | At least **€30,000** for medical expenses including hospitalisation and emergency medical treatment | ☐ |
| **Geographic coverage** | Valid in the **entire Schengen area** (all 29 member states) — explicit mention or a stated list of countries | ☐ |
| **Repatriation** | Covers **emergency medical repatriation** to home country | ☐ |
| **Mortal remains repatriation** | Covers transport of remains in case of death | ☐ |
| **Validity period** | Covers **from the first day of intended stay to the last day**, inclusive. Including ≥1 day on either side as a buffer is recommended | ☐ |
| **Applicant name** | Your name on the certificate **exactly matches your passport** | ☐ |
| **Currency** | Stated in **euros** OR clearly converted at a stated exchange rate | ☐ |
| **Insurer is authorised** | Insurer is licensed to operate in the EU OR is a recognised international insurer (not a no-name aggregator) | ☐ |
| **Certificate language** | French or English (not the policy details — just the **certificate page** you bring) | ☐ |

---

## Where to buy (categories, not endorsements)

The market has three rough tiers:

| Tier | Examples (search yourself; market changes) | Trade-offs |
|---|---|---|
| **Standalone Schengen-visa insurance** | Insurers that exclusively serve visa applicants. Often €15–40 for a single trip. Cheapest. | Certificate is purpose-made for Schengen visa applications — strong format. Usually limited to medical + repatriation; no trip cancellation. |
| **General travel insurance with Schengen cover** | Most consumer travel-insurance brands offer Schengen-compliant policies. Often £30–80. | Broader coverage (cancellations, lost luggage). Make sure the certificate page explicitly says "Schengen visa compliant" — the underlying policy may be compliant but the **printable certificate** may not state it clearly. |
| **Annual multi-trip policies** | Annual cover for frequent travellers. £80–250/year. | Cheapest per-trip if you'll travel multiple times. Same certificate-clarity caveat as standalone. |

**This project does not endorse specific providers.** Search "Schengen visa insurance compliant" and compare. Read recent reviews — providers go in and out of compliance.

---

## When to buy

| Sequence option | Why people choose it |
|---|---|
| **Buy before Phase 1 (France-Visas)** | You can include the certificate details in the France-Visas form (slightly more complete application). Risk: if the trip dates shift, you may need to amend the policy. |
| **Buy after Phase 1, before Phase 2** | The trip dates from France-Visas guide your policy dates. Most applicants do this. |
| **Buy 1–2 days before TLScontact appointment** | Last-minute; risks running into payment / certificate-generation issues. Not recommended. |

**Buy at least 5 working days before your appointment** to allow for:
- Insurer technical delays in issuing the certificate
- Time to fix any name/date typos
- Time to print + verify all fields match what your application says

---

## Verification checklist (do this when the certificate arrives)

- [ ] PDF / printed certificate is readable in full
- [ ] Your name appears exactly as on your passport (accents, hyphens, capitalisation)
- [ ] Policy dates cover **at minimum** your trip dates (+1 day buffer each side is safer)
- [ ] Coverage amount stated in **EUR**, ≥ €30,000 explicit
- [ ] **"Schengen area"** is mentioned in the geographic scope
- [ ] **Repatriation** is explicitly mentioned (not just "emergency assistance")
- [ ] Insurer logo + contact details visible
- [ ] No watermarks saying "specimen" or "draft"
- [ ] Print 2 copies (one for TLScontact submission, one to keep as proof for in-person check)

---

## Family / multi-applicant policies

If the policy covers multiple people (family policy):

- [ ] All applicants' names are on the certificate
- [ ] Each applicant gets a copy (TLScontact files one per applicant)
- [ ] The coverage amount applies **per person**, not pooled — confirm with the insurer

If each applicant has a separate policy, that's fine too. Just bring each person's certificate clearly labelled.

---

## Common pitfalls

| Pitfall | How to avoid |
|---|---|
| Buying a non-Schengen-compliant policy from a price-aggregator | Always check the certificate explicitly says "Schengen" + "€30,000+" + "repatriation." If the certificate is silent on any of these, **call the insurer** for an explicit confirmation letter. |
| Policy dates don't cover the buffer days | If you arrive 23 May 06:00 and leave 28 May 22:00, your policy should cover **at least** 22 May to 29 May. Tight day-of-edges trigger admin questions. |
| Currency stated in GBP only | The Schengen rule is €30,000. A "£25,000" certificate is **not automatically compliant** — even though £25,000 ≈ €29,000+ today, the currency conversion isn't theirs to do. Buy in EUR or with explicit EUR equivalence. |
| Name typo | Some insurers' systems auto-format names (e.g. "MCKENZIE" → "Mckenzie"). If the result doesn't match your passport, **contact the insurer to fix** before printing. |
| Policy bought but not yet issued by appointment day | Some insurers issue certificates 24–48h after payment. **Don't buy the night before.** |
